content:
Requirement R07 (input): Report Surveillance Event. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to report a surveillance event as it happens..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-07.1, F-07.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-07.<F>.1, Be-07.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-07.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent restated:** Enable the pilot to report a surveillance event to C2 at the moment it occurs, using Touch and Keyboard.

Function candidates:

**F-07.1 — Capture and transmit a time-critical event report.**
The teleology: get a surveillance-event report from pilot to C2. This is the report-authoring-and-send goal — the artefact exists to convert the pilot's observation into a transmittable intel package. Distinct from R05 (intel report) only in trigger context (event-driven, in-the-moment); functionally very close, so worth flagging: **the Be/S here could largely share R05's compose-and-transmit machinery.**

**F-07.2 — Mark the event instant with minimal pilot action.**
The teleology: seize the transient moment — one-action logging that timestamps/geo-tags the event without pulling the pilot into a composition task. Different goal: not "author a report" but "don't lose the moment." Prioritizes speed of capture over report richness.

**F-07.3 — Pre-declare the awaited event so occurrence is one confirmation.**
The teleology: since surveillance (UC 3.2) involves waiting for a known trigger in a known area, the artefact's purpose here is to arm an expected event beforehand so that at occurrence the pilot confirms rather than composes. Different goal: shifting cognitive load ahead of the time-critical instant.

My recommendation: **F-07.1** as the primary, because the use case (3.2.3/3.2.4) is explicitly "identifies event occurrence and reports it" — an authoring-and-send function. But F-07.2 is a genuinely strong contender given the "as it happens" phrasing and cockpit workload constraints; if speed-of-capture dominates over report content, that's the truer function.

Which do you want to close on?
F-07.1 is best here. This requirement is mostly the same as R05, but instead of filling a full form, it should be generated automatically once certain conditions are met.

Agreed on **F-07.1**, with a sharper reading: the function isn't "author a report" but **auto-generate a surveillance-event report on trigger and transmit it to C2** — pilot action is confirmation/dispatch, not composition. The report body is machine-assembled (timestamp, geo, sensor context) when conditions are met; the pilot's role is to authorize send.

This keeps it firmly distinct from R05 (pilot-authored, full compose) while reusing R05's transmit/validation/send machinery downstream.

**Flag:** the send-path Structure (validation gate + dual-confirm transmit overlay) is a strong reuse candidate from R05. What's new in R07 is the auto-generation/trigger side, not the transmission.

**F-07.1 — Auto-generate a surveillance-event report on trigger condition and transmit it to C2.** Closed.

Moving to Behaviour.

The system should receive and monitor parameters and trigger a surveillance report once conditions are met.
The user should be also be able to add some predefined data to each "event trigger" such as a title and description.

Note the scope expansion: beyond auto-generate-and-send, R07 now includes a **pre-configuration** aspect — the pilot attaches predefined metadata (title, description) to each event trigger *before* it fires, so the auto-generated report carries meaningful labels. That's still within F-07.1 (the trigger-side is what's new vs R05); the metadata authoring is a lightweight pre-arm task, not full composition.

Behaviour candidates (Touch and Keyboard fixed modalities):

**Be-07.1.1 — Touch-only pathway.**
Pilot opens an event-trigger panel on WAD, taps to create a trigger, taps into title/description fields and enters text via on-screen keypad (touch), taps to set/select the monitored parameter condition. System continuously monitors incoming parameters; on threshold match it auto-assembles the report (timestamp/geo/sensor + pilot's title/description) and surfaces it in the R05-reused send overlay. Pilot dual-confirms send by touch. Auto-send-on-trigger optional via a touch toggle.

**Be-07.1.2 — Keyboard-only pathway.**
Same flow driven by bezel OSS + UCP: OSS to create/select a trigger slot, UCP alphanumeric for title/description, rotary/OSS to step and set the parameter condition. Monitoring and auto-generation identical. On trigger, report appears in send overlay; pilot confirms/dispatches via OSS press-and-confirm.

**Be-07.1.3 — Mixed pathway (adds real value).**
Pre-arm split by natural fit: UCP keyboard for text-heavy metadata (title/description), Touch for spatial/selection (pick trigger, set condition on a value widget). At trigger time the auto-report surfaces and either modality confirms send. This adds value because metadata is inherently alphanumeric (keyboard-native) while condition-setting is selection/spatial (touch-native) — the mix is faster than either alone without locking any sub-step to one modality (redundancy rule still holds: each pathway above can complete standalone).

**Recommendation:** carry all three, with **Be-07.1.3** as the realistic operational path and .1/.2 preserved to satisfy modality-complete redundancy.

One design question before closing: the **monitoring/trigger-evaluation engine itself is not a modality behaviour** — it's a system-internal function. The Behaviour layer here covers only (a) pilot arming/labeling the trigger and (b) pilot confirming/dispatching the auto-report. Agreed to treat the monitoring as internal, with modalities only on the arm and dispatch ends?

Have both input systems be usable for using this system. Remember this for the next requirements. No input should be only touch or only keyboard. As well as being both able to start on one pathway and end on another.
For this requirement, the user creates a trigger, adds title/description fields, sets the monitored parameters and arms the event.

Understood, and I'll carry this forward as a standing rule for all subsequent requirements:

**Standing rule:** No pathway is single-modality-locked. Every sub-step (create trigger, enter title/description, set parameters, arm, confirm-dispatch) is completable by Touch *or* Keyboard, and the pilot can switch modalities mid-task (start on one, finish on another). Redundancy is per-step, not per-pathway.

So R07 has **one interleaved behaviour**, not three separate modality pathways. Restating the arm-side task per your scope: create trigger → add title/description → set monitored parameters → arm. Then system monitors internally; on trigger it auto-generates and surfaces the report for dispatch.

**Be-07.1.1 — Interleaved arm-and-dispatch behaviour.**
- **Create trigger:** Touch tap on WAD trigger list *or* bezel OSS to add a slot — either creates the same trigger object.
- **Title/description:** Touch on-screen keypad *or* UCP alphanumeric; a field opened by touch can be completed on UCP and vice versa (shared field buffer, no lock).
- **Set monitored parameters:** Touch value widget *or* rotary/OSS stepping — both write the same condition object, gated by a single validation.
- **Arm:** Touch *or* bezel press-and-confirm toggle; armed state persists across modalities (consistent with R03 armed-state persistence).
- **Internal monitoring:** system-side, non-modal — evaluates incoming parameters against the armed condition.
- **On trigger:** auto-assembled report (timestamp/geo/sensor + pilot title/description) surfaces in the R05-reused send overlay; pilot dual-confirms dispatch via Touch *or* OSS, again switchable mid-confirm.

**Reuse flags:** dispatch end reuses R05's validation gate + dual-confirm send overlay; arm toggle reuses R03's press-and-confirm + persistent-armed-state pattern; the title/description field mirrors R05's interleaved touch/keyboard entry.

Confirm the monitoring stays internal (modalities only on arm and dispatch), and I'll close Be-07.1.1 and move to Structure.

Monitoring is the system's job. Also, the user should be able to delete/edit already present triggers. So with that, onto structure.
It shouldn't be much different from R05's structure.

**Be-07.1.1** closed — monitoring internal; adding trigger management (create/edit/delete) to the arm-side task set.

Structure candidates. All build on R05's overlay/validation/send machinery; the delta is a trigger-list manager and the arm control.

**S-07.1.1.1 — R05 overlay extended with a trigger-list panel.**
- Reuse R05's WAD compose-and-transmit overlay as the base container.
- Add a **trigger-list panel** (left region): scrollable list of trigger objects, each row = title + condition summary + armed-state indicator. Row actions: create (Touch tap "+" / bezel OSS), select, edit, delete (Touch swipe-or-button / OSS).
- **Detail sub-panel** (right region): title/description fields (Touch keypad *or* UCP, shared buffer per R05 entry model); parameter-condition widget (Touch value entry *or* rotary/OSS stepping); single flight-envelope-style validation gate (reused R01/R05 gate) before a trigger can be armed.
- **ARM toggle:** press-and-confirm, dual-input, armed-state persistent — reuses R03 pattern.
- **On trigger:** auto-report surfaces in R05's dual-confirm send region; dispatch by Touch or OSS.
- Bezel OSS map: [+ NEW] [EDIT] [DELETE] [ARM] [CONFIRM]; rotary for list navigation and value stepping.

**S-07.1.1.2 — Reuse R06's list/detail pattern instead of R05's compose overlay.**
- R06 already built a WAD **list/detail panel backed by a single order store**. Mirror that: trigger-list = list side, trigger-editor = detail side, backed by a **single trigger store** (analogous to R06's order store) that also drives the armed-state indicator and the auto-report generation.
- Send/dispatch still reuses R05's validation + dual-confirm.
- Advantage: consistent list/detail interaction already familiar from R06; the trigger store cleanly separates authored config from the auto-generated report.

**S-07.1.1.3 — Minimal: single trigger-editor overlay, no persistent list.**
- One overlay editing one trigger at a time; edit/delete via re-opening the active trigger. No list panel.
- Cheapest reuse of R05 (nearly identical structure) but weakest for managing multiple concurrent triggers — and UC 3.2 plausibly involves more than one awaited event. I'd not recommend this given the create/edit/delete requirement.

**Recommendation: S-07.1.1.2** — it satisfies edit/delete/multiple-trigger management via the proven R06 list/detail + single-store pattern, while reusing R05 for dispatch. It's the closest to "not much different from R05" while properly handling trigger persistence and management.

**Reuse flags:** R05 (send overlay, validation gate, interleaved entry), R06 (list/detail + single store), R03 (armed-state persistent toggle). Genuinely new: the trigger store's link to internal monitoring and auto-report generation.
S-07.1.1.2. is best here, but the event should be sent without any confirmation, instantly once the conditions are met.

**S-07.1.1.2** closed, with one modification that changes the dispatch model:

**Auto-dispatch on trigger — no confirmation.** Once monitoring detects conditions met, the auto-assembled report (timestamp/geo/sensor + authored title/description) is transmitted to C2 **instantly**, with no pilot dual-confirm step. This drops R05's dual-confirm send gate from the trigger-fire path.

Consequences to lock in:
- **Validation moves entirely to arm-time.** Since there's no send-time confirmation, the flight-envelope-style validation gate now runs before **ARM** — a trigger cannot be armed unless its condition and metadata are valid. This is the only gate; the dispatch itself is unattended.
- **The R05 send overlay is no longer reused as an interactive dispatch surface.** R07 reuses R05 only for the underlying transmit-to-C2 mechanism (the plumbing), not its confirm UI.
- **Post-send feedback replaces pre-send confirmation.** The pilot needs to know a report fired unattended — so a notification on dispatch (reusing R02/R06's multi-channel alert framework: notification strip + audio ping) informing "event report sent to C2." This is output-only, not a confirmation gate.

Final structure:
- Trigger-list + detail editor (R06 list/detail pattern), backed by a **single trigger store**.
- Create/edit/delete triggers via Touch or bezel OSS (interleaved, switchable).
- Title/description via Touch keypad or UCP (shared buffer); parameter-condition via Touch widget or rotary/OSS.
- **Arm-time validation gate** (reused R01/R05 gate) — the sole gate.
- ARM press-and-confirm toggle, persistent armed-state (R03 pattern).
- Internal monitoring → **instant unattended transmit** to C2 (R05 transmit plumbing).
- **Dispatch notification** via R02/R06 alert framework (output-only).

Confirm this and R07 is fully specified across all three layers.

R07 fully specified:

**F-07.1** — Auto-generate a surveillance-event report on trigger condition and transmit it to C2 (pilot arms/labels; dispatch is unattended).

**Be-07.1.1** — Interleaved, non-modality-locked arm-and-manage behaviour: create/edit/delete triggers, enter title/description, set monitored parameters, arm — each sub-step completable by Touch or Keyboard and switchable mid-task. Monitoring is internal; on trigger, instant unattended transmit; post-send notification informs the pilot.

**S-07.1.1.2** — R06 list/detail pattern backed by a single trigger store; create/edit/delete via Touch or bezel OSS; title/description via Touch keypad or UCP (shared buffer); condition via Touch widget or rotary/OSS; **arm-time validation gate** (sole gate, reused R01/R05); ARM press-and-confirm toggle with persistent armed-state (R03); internal monitoring → instant unattended transmit (R05 plumbing); dispatch notification via R02/R06 alert framework (output-only).

**Reuse ledger:** R01/R05 validation gate; R05 transmit plumbing; R06 list/detail + single-store; R03 armed-state toggle; R02/R06 alert framework.

**Standing rule recorded for future requirements:** no single-modality-locked pathways; every sub-step Touch-or-Keyboard completable and mid-task switchable.

Ready for R08 when you are.
